# Incident 1361: Waymo Autonomous Vehicle Reportedly Struck Child Near Elementary School in Santa Monica, California

- Incident date: 2026-01-23
- Source: AI Incident Database (input to the MIT AI Incident Tracker), https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/1361

A Waymo driverless vehicle reportedly struck a child near an elementary school in Santa Monica, California during school drop-off hours. According to filings with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the child allegedly sustained minor injuries. The vehicle was purportedly operating on Waymo's 5th Generation Automated Driving System without a human safety driver. Waymo reported the incident to federal regulators, who subsequently opened an investigation.

Alleged implicated AI systems: pedestrian detection system, autonomous vehicle perception system, autonomous vehicle decision-making system, automated braking system, 5th-generation Waymo Driver. Harmed: unnamed elementary school student, pedestrians, minors.

severity_hint: severe/catastrophic: physical harm to a minor (MIT harm scale 4-5 of 5)

- Incident date: 2026-01-18
- Source: AI Incident Database (input to the MIT AI Incident Tracker), https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/1367

In Spokane, Washington, a Spokane Transit Authority double-decker bus was reportedly routed by its onboard navigation/CAD mapping system onto Cedar Street and hit a low-clearance railroad viaduct, shearing the upper deck. Of 10 people aboard, seven were reportedly hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. STA reportedly later warned operators not to use CAD maps for routing and pulled double-deckers from service pending an investigation; the driver was cited for negligent driving.

Alleged implicated AI systems: CAD/navigation routing technology, unidentified STA onboard CAD/navigation routing software. Harmed: STA bus passengers and personnel.

- Incident date: 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-04
- Source: AI Incident Database (input to the MIT AI Incident Tracker), https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/1646

Suspected China-linked hackers reportedly used a multi-agent framework built on Hermes and OpenClaw to compromise Taiwanese government systems. The agents reportedly compromised 85 credentials and used persistent access to connected systems to exfiltrate more than 2,564 personnel records. Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs later confirmed an overseas AI-assisted campaign against government agencies ("first-of-a-kind breach"), without attributing it to China.

Alleged implicated AI systems: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, LLMs, AI agent systems. Harmed: Taiwanese government agencies/employees, Ministry of Justice, privacy, national security.

# Incident 1687: Anthropic-Designated GTG-87001 Weapons Cell in Northern Yemen Reportedly Used Claude Code to Develop Missile Guidance Software

- Incident date: 2026-09-10 (first public disclosure; activity spanned 12/2025-08/2026)
- Source: AI Incident Database (input to the MIT AI Incident Tracker), https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/1687

Anthropic reported that a northern Yemen-based weapons cell, designated GTG-87001, used Claude Code across three weapons programs to develop guidance, navigation, and control software. The actors reportedly test-fired a guided rocket that appeared to fail, then returned to Claude for failure analysis. Anthropic said it banned associated accounts, shared threat intelligence with partners, and strengthened safeguards. # Hugging Face security incident disclosure — July 2026 (published 2026-07-16)

- Source: Hugging Face blog, https://huggingface.co/blog/security-incident-july-2026
- Type: security incident / postmortem (production intrusion)

Hugging Face detected and responded to an intrusion into part of its production infrastructure, driven end to end by an autonomous AI agent system, and detected/dissected largely with AI of its own.

## What happened
- Initial access via the data-processing pipeline: a malicious dataset abused two code-execution paths (a remote-code dataset loader and a template-injection in a dataset configuration) to run code on a processing worker.
- Escalation to node-level access, harvesting of cloud and cluster credentials, and lateral movement into several internal clusters over a weekend.
- The campaign was run by an autonomous agent framework (built on an agentic security-research harness; LLM unknown), executing many thousands of actions across a swarm of short-lived sandboxes, with self-migrating C2 staged on public services — the "agentic attacker" scenario.
- Impact: unauthorized access to a limited set of internal datasets and several service credentials. No evidence of tampering with public, user-facing models, datasets, or Spaces; software supply chain (container images, published packages) verified clean.

## Response
- Closed the dataset code-execution paths; eradicated the foothold and rebuilt compromised nodes; revoked/rotated affected credentials and tokens plus precautionary secret rotation; deployed guardrails and stricter cluster admission controls; improved detection so high-severity signals page a responder in minutes; engaged outside forensics; reported to law enforcement.

## Detection & forensics (AI on defense)
- An LLM-based triage pipeline over security telemetry surfaced the anomaly; correlation of signals flagged the compromise.
- LLM-driven analysis agents ran over the full attacker action log (17,000+ recorded events) to reconstruct the timeline, extract IoCs, map touched credentials, and separate real impact from decoys — hours instead of days.
- Asymmetry lesson: hosted frontier models' safety guardrails blocked submitting real attack payloads, so forensics ran on the open-weight zai-org/GLM-5.2 on HF's own infrastructure — keeping attacker data and credentials in-environment. Lesson: have a capable self-hosted model vetted before an incident.

Recommended community action: rotate access tokens and review recent account activity; report concerns to security@huggingface.co.
severity_hint: severe: autonomous AI-agent intrusion into Hugging Face production infrastructure; limited internal datasets and service credentials accessed; no public model/dataset/Space tampering; supply chain verified clean (MIT harm scale 4 of 5, privacy & security)
